correctness.rationale: Every endomorphism has f(v+tz)=Av+(ell(v)+ct)z with omega(Au,Av)=c omega(u,v). Multiplier nonzero forces a full-rank conformal symplectic map; multiplier zero gives isotropic image rank at most m. Direct isotropic-frame counting yields I_mr, surjective-map counting gives B_mr, rowspace membership of ell yields q^r vs q^(2m)-q^r rank split. Ratios B_r/B_(r-1) decrease and have minimum order q^m, allowing an explicit first-order deficiency calculation; automorphism contribution is exponentially lower in m squared. Direct independent enumeration over (m,q)=(1,2),(1,3),(2,2) reproduced full spectra. Error bounds require fixed q, and no experiment is treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The rank-refined size of an algebra endomorphism monoid is a natural isomorphism-invariant quantitative structure. For the entire Heisenberg family over every finite field, the theorem completely classifies attainable ranks, exposes a dimension-growing forbidden interval between the singular ranks and full rank, and identifies the high-dimensional dominant rank with sharp first-order probability deficiency. These are not supplied by a mere normal form, a textbook basis substitution, or an idempotent-only census; the precise fixed-q asymptotic is relevant to generic singular homomorphisms.
